THE HOST/DEVICE DESCRIPTOR SEAM, as a gate rather than a comment.
Two independent descriptor parsers will drift. The Rust one in `me` and the Go
one that ships on the SeedHammer II are the same question asked in two
languages, and the direction that matters is asymmetric: a host that admits
what the device refuses packs a payload the device cannot read -- an engraved
plate for a wallet that will not load.
THE INVARIANT: host_admits(input) => device_admits(canonical(input)).
It is stated over the CANONICAL string, not the input, and that is deliberate
(SPEC_descriptor_input.md S7 requirement 4). Two row classes make the
input-level form wrong:
* the S4.6 whitespace rows -- the host trims and normalises CRLF before the
cascade, so it is deliberately WIDER than the device on the raw bytes. It
is safe only because what gets PACKED is `canonical`, never the operator's
file, and a `sysw` record cannot contain a newline by construction.
* bluewallet/no-derivation-header -- device-ACCEPTED as INPUT, while its own
canonical re-encoding does not re-parse. An input-level assertion is blind
to the one row class the invariant exists for.
So: for every host_admits=true row the Go test parses `canonical`, requires
ACCEPT, and requires the re-encoding of that parse to equal `canonical` (a
fixed point). A row where the host is wider and `canonical` is absent is a
defect both tests reject.
WHAT EACH COLUMN MEANS, exactly:
host_admits    -- S5.2's classification predicate: `me` would pack this input
as a `Descriptor` record. NOT "me's cascade parses it"
(`me` parses `multi`, and `multi` is host_admits=false) and
NOT "some --as succeeds" (--as md1 succeeds on `multi`).
device_admits  -- Go: nonstandard.OutputDescriptor accepts the INPUT. The
scan door, nothing else. Present on EVERY row: S2's
convergence fix (the `!= 4` fingerprint guard) removed the
one parse panic that made the predicate unevaluable, so no
row omits the column and requirement 5's non-vacuity count
skips none.
format         -- the branch of S4's cascade that `me` MATCHED. Read
STRICTLY as "the branch that SUCCEEDED" (S4.1: first branch
that succeeds wins), so a row `me` refuses AT the cascade
carries "none" -- including every BlueWallet shape S4.2
narrows and every refused S4.5 promotion, whose branch fails
for `me` even where the device's parser accepts. A row whose
cascade SUCCEEDED and whose refusal comes from S4.7's
admission predicate or S5.3's representability limits keeps
its branch name. That split is the column's information: it
says whether the refusal is the parser's or the profile's.
S6's "the branch the input most RESEMBLES" is a different,
diagnostic-selection rule and does not feed this column.
md1_admits     -- whether `me sysw pack --as md1` carries this input. An
INDEPENDENT axis, not a qualifier on host_admits: the
`multi` row is host_admits=false / md1_admits=true, and
/0/* is host_admits=true / md1_admits=false.
(RETIRED in S2: `sysw_class`, a four-row SAMPLE of the device classifier's
answer. Both suites now assert the classifier EXHAUSTIVELY, from the columns
already here: for every single-line row, Classify(input) == Descriptor iff
host_admits and Unknown otherwise, and for every host_admits row
Classify(canonical) == Descriptor. A derived rule over 59 rows cannot drift
from a hand-stated value on 4, and it has no input-vs-canonical ambiguity.)
canonical      -- REQUIRED wherever host_admits is true: the re-encoded
descriptor string both parsers must produce.
device_probe   -- the row's input PANICS the device, and at which site. The
only surviving value is "panic:encode" (S4.2 defects 1-2):
parse ACCEPTS and Descriptor.Encode() panics, so the Go test
may parse but must NOT call Encode. A panic would CRASH the
suite rather than fail it -- a false-signal shape. S2 retired
the "panic:parse" marker with the parse panic it named: the
fingerprint guard is `!= 4` now and the parser errors
cleanly, so no row bars the Go test from OutputDescriptor.
covers         -- which S7 required-row bullets this row discharges. The
coverage manifest below is NORMATIVE and is counted, not
read.
gate_open / outcome / refusal_row / exit_code
-- the four gate fields, REQUIRED on every `gate`-tagged row
and absent elsewhere. S5.1's gate states an intent and two
invariants; these rows are its executable precision, and
where any reading of the prose disagrees with a row, the
row is the answer. Asserted by the RUST test only -- the
gate is `me`'s surface and the device has no counterpart.
address_0/1    -- receive addresses at indices 0 and 1. The Go test derives
each through address.Receive on the parsed INPUT wherever
device_admits is true; the Rust test derives each through
the md1 round trip wherever md1_admits is true. On a row
where both hold, the two routes are asserted to the SAME
value -- which is what S5.3(a')'s materialisation claim
means at the address layer.
wallet_id      -- the WalletPolicyId fingerprint, asserted by BOTH suites,
each computing it from its own implementation. The F-212
class -- a cross-language identity divergence no per-repo
test can see -- made into a standing gate. Carried by
MULTISIG rows at the device-default use-site only: that is
the Go route's measured domain, because md.EncodeMultisig
hard-codes <0;1>/* and has no single-sig arm.
md_descriptor_contains
-- a substring the `md descriptor` read-back of the encoded
set must contain. The pin on the `multi` row is
"wsh(multi(" and NOT "multi(", because "sortedmulti("
CONTAINS "multi(" and the shorter pin passes on the
multi -> sortedmulti mutant's own read-back.
A MISTYPED VECTOR FAILS LOUDLY. The codex32 file uses a `chars` count for this;
this file uses a per-row sha256 of `input`, because a descriptor is long enough
that a character count would not catch a transcription error inside an xpub.

The minima sum to 89 tag-slots; the fifteen shared S4.5 rows absorb 15 of
`gate`'s slots and the original overlap pair absorbs 2 more, so the file
carries at least 89 - 17 = 72 PHYSICAL rows. A row may carry more than one tag
only where the manifest names it, and `covers` entries are distinct within a
row -- so a dropped row cannot be counted around by retagging or duplication.
`refusal_rows` is the slug vocabulary the gate rows' `refusal_row` field draws
from: one entry per S6 data row (35), so the per-row text tests and the gate
rows cannot drift apart by inventing different names for the same refusal.

build, and no build state refuses it any more -- and the remaining rows are
renumbered to match S6's table.
